messages:
maria: FYI bringing up a new embed candidate (arbor-v1) — baseline float32 recall@10 on our multilingual holdout was 0.821, after our standard int8 pertensor quant pipeline it dropped to 0.687. UMAP shows obvious cluster fragmentation for pt/ja docs :thinking_face:

junaid: ugh. do we know if the quant step is applied before or after l2-normalize in the offline pipeline? that ordering kills cosine similarity if wrong.

maria: it's currently quantized post-encode but pre-normalize (we used our legacy disk-quant pipeline). code snippet we ran:```python
emb = model.encode(doc)
quant_emb = quantize_pt(emb)  # per-tensor int8
final = l2_normalize(quant_emb)
```

sylvie: that could explain it. recommend two quick checks: 1) quantize after l2-normalize and 2) try per-channel symmetric quant (int8_pc) with clamp calib. per-channel often preserves relative geometry better for embeddings.

ryan: also check whitening/mean-centering pipeline. we sometimes see PCA axis flip after quant which splits clusters into rings on umap. small numbers: pre-quant silhouette=0.13, post-quant silhouette=0.03 for the same holdout.

katie: can we run a 5k-sample AB where: A = quant after normalize (pertensor), B = quant after normalize (per-channel)? i can queue on /eng-ml-eval.

maria: yes please. job definition I used:```bash
python eval/recall.py \
  --model arbor-v1 \
  --quant int8_pt \
  --holdout multilingual_holdout.json \
  --k 10 \
  --batch 128 \
  --whiten false
```
swap int8_pt -> int8_pc and toggle --normalize-before-quant true for the runs.

junaid: +1 also try clamp calibration with 2k samples vs 20k samples. sometimes the tail tokens skew scales.

eval-bot: quick sanity job finished (5k samples):
- float32 recall@10 = 0.821
- int8_pt quant AFTER normalize recall@10 = 0.703 (+0.016 vs earlier)
- int8_pc quant AFTER normalize recall@10 = 0.799 (much closer)
- silhouette (umap 2D) float32 = 0.13, int8_pc = 0.11, int8_pt = 0.03
(attach: /artifacts/4267891234/umap_grid.png)

sylvie: nice, per-channel after normalize looks promising. still want to run a longer 50k-sample run with whitening on to see recall@1 drift (short queries).

ryan: curious if storage format (packed int8 vs 6-bit blocked) matters for our retrieval stack — will the indexer treat PC quant differently? @katie can you check indexer compatibility?

katie: indexer handles per-channel just fine, but we need to update the ingest script to set "scale_per_channel": true. i'll add a small migration.

maria: action items: 1) katie to update ingest and run 50k PC-after-normalize + whitening job (owner: katie) 2) junaid to run clamp calib sweep (2k/20k) and share scales (owner: junaid) 3) sylvie to prepare a short eval note comparing recall@1/5/10 + silhouette + few UMAPs (owner: sylvie). i'll draft a rollout playbook assuming int8_pc passes.

junaid: planning to run calib sweep this afternoon, will post numbers.

katie: queued 50k job — estimate 2h. tagging this for follow-up in tomorrow standup. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — great triage. if int8_pc + normalize + whitening gets us within 1-2% of float32 on recall@10 and keeps clusters intact, we can proceed with quantized deploy for arbor-v1 on dedicated pools.

eval-bot: follow-up results (50k, with whitening):
- float32 recall@10 = 0.821
- int8_pc after-normalize + whitening recall@10 = 0.812 (delta -0.009)
- recall@1 float32 = 0.612, int8_pc = 0.604
- silhouette float32 = 0.13, int8_pc = 0.115
summary: acceptable degradation, cluster geometry largely preserved.

maria: perfect — i'll update the onboarding doc and open a canary rollout PR. thanks all :)
